title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes try to axiomatize a tame ('modérée') topology. The main objects appear to be the following. M is a set of strata or cells, ordered by ≤ ('is a face/sub-stratum of'). F is the set of 'figures' (stratified compact pieces), with: Omb(F), the support ('ombre'); F̃, the 'déploiement', i.e. the poset of strata of F; refinement F' ≪ F; restriction F'_L of a refinement to a sub-figure L; and the intersection figure L = F.G. There are two relations. X ≭ Y is a 'good relative position' relation (intersection, ≭, as it appears used here). F ‖ G is compatibility, which by p.15 means: for all X'∈F̃, Y'∈G̃, X'≭Y'. The page has three parts.

(1) Proposition, merging p.14–15. With F≭G, L = F∩G, F'≪F and G'≪G: F'‖G' ⇔ F'_L ‖ G'_L. So compatibility of refinements is decided entirely over the common part L. The Corollary 'At D0' says compatibility is stable under refinement: F‖G, F'≪F, G'≪G ⇒ F'‖G'. The margin points to Cor. 2 (lemma 2').

(2) Axiom/criterion 'At pol', a compatibility criterion apparently for polyhedral-type strata. Take X, Y ∈ M, not assumed compatible. Let L = sup of the Z in X̃∩Ỹ, i.e. the union of the common faces. Assume (a) every pair of strata X'≪X, Y'≪Y lying off L (X'_L = Y'_L = ∅) is compatible, X'‖Y'. Assume also (b) L = ∅ or L ∈ M, i.e. {X,Y} has an inf in (M,≤), so the common faces have a largest element. Then X≭Y. The margin stresses that no closure axiom (e.g. stability of M under intersection) is assumed here beyond At D0.

(3) Proposition, assuming At pol. Take F, G ∈ F, with L = F.G. Then F≭G if two conditions hold. (i) For all strata X∈F̃, Y∈G̃ that are bounded below in M, X∩Y ∈ M; that is, X̃∩Ỹ is empty or has a greatest element. This is the 'two cells meet in a common face' condition of polyhedral/regular CW complexes. (ii) Refined strata of F and G lying off L are pairwise compatible.

The theme is a local-to-global criterion for good relative position of stratified figures. Good position is checked (a) combinatorially, on the face posets via existence of infs, and (b) by compatibility away from the common part. It serves the goal of building a category of 'figures' that is closed under intersection and common refinement. 'Voir validité en C' marks this as still to be checked in the intended model category C (semi-analytic/semi-algebraic/PL). The next page adds At spéc (drop the finiteness condition (b)), At D, At C and At fil (filtered sups of refinements, with gluing of refinements), and the implications among these axioms.
errors: Nothing is proved on this page. 'At pol' is posed as an axiom/criterion whose validity in the model category C is explicitly left open ('Voir validité en C', 'Voir la validité de la proposition').

The meaning of X'_L = ∅ is ambiguous: X' as a stratum of a refinement avoiding L, versus a whole refinement with empty restriction. Under the 'whole refinement' reading, hypothesis (ii) would be nearly vacuous, so the stratum reading is presumably intended.

In the final Proposition, L = F.G is formed without assuming F≭G. It is not explained in what sense F.G exists for figures not yet known to be in good position; p.17's diagram Omb(F)∩Omb(G) → Omb(L) suggests L may be only a figure inside the set-theoretic intersection.

ideas.what: Compatibility of refinements of two figures is detected over their intersection: F'‖G' ⇔ F'_L‖G'_L, and compatibility is stable under refinement (At D0).
ideas.modern_name: Locality of compatible / common refinements of stratifications (cf. Whitney/o-minimal stratifications compatible with subsets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); for the tame setting, o-minimal cell decomposition theory (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme of 'topologie modérée' is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, without these axioms.

ideas.what: Criterion 'At pol': two cells are in good position if their common faces have a largest element (inf exists in the face poset) and their refined cells off that common face are compatible.
ideas.modern_name: Intersection condition of polyhedral / regular cell complexes (two cells meet in a common face), stated as a local-to-global axiom
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology / combinatorial topology (polyhedral complexes)

ideas.what: Axiomatic hierarchy of tameness axioms (At D0, At D, At C, At pol, At spéc, At fil) on a poset of strata with refinement and compatibility relations.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; cf. o-minimal structures, Shiota's 'tame' (X-)sets, Lojasiewicz/Hironaka subanalytic stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (Tame Topology and o-minimal structures, 1998); Shiota (1997)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only gives the motivation; the axiomatics appear unpublished.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a combinatorial-poset criterion for good relative position of tame cells (existence of inf of common faces plus compatibility away from the common face). He leaves its validity in the intended model category C (semi-analytic/PL/o-minimal) unchecked. Whether such a criterion holds in o-minimal or subanalytic settings, and whether it suffices to build a category of figures stable under intersection, is an explicit open thread.
missed.quote: Supposons de plus que L=∅ ou L∈M i.e. {X,Y} admet un Inf dans (M,≤). Alors X ≭ Y. … Voir : la validité de la proposition
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give an intrinsic, poset-level axiomatization of 'tame' stratified spaces. This is relevant to current work on exit-path categories and stratified homotopy theory, and to the still-open goal of a foundational tame topology in the sense of the Esquisse.

missed.claim: Compatibility is treated via the face posets (déploiements) and infs in (M,≤), rather than point-set geometry. This implicitly links tame topology to the combinatorics of regular CW/poset models (face posets, Björner-type regular cell complexes).
missed.quote: X∩Y∈M, i.e. X̃∩Ỹ est vide ou a un plus grand élément
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests describing tame stratified spaces by their face posets with an 'intersection = face' axiom. This aligns with later stratified homotopy theory (exit-path ∞-categories) but is not carried out there as an axiom system.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds detailed, unpublished axiomatics for Grothendieck's tame topology programme: refinement, compatibility and a poset-theoretic criterion for good position. The individual mathematics (cells meeting in common faces, locality of compatible refinements) is classical. The novelty lies in the unfinished axiomatic framework itself, which is known only in outline from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Left top margin probably reads 'cf aussi Cor. 2 (lemme 2')' with 'V.' before 'Cor 2'.
'X'_L = 0, Y'_L = 0' should read X'_L = ∅, Y'_L = ∅, consistent with the later (ii).
The title of At pol after 'Critère de compatibilité pour' is hard to read: something like 'strates/cellules' then 'polyédraux' rather than 'polyidéaux'.
The long left margin note is roughly 'On ne suppose pas ici que M soit stable par intersections … (pour) … (At D0)', explaining that no intersection-closure axiom is assumed.
'{+par minoration [?] ou [?]+}' is better read as an insertion '(i.e. minoré)' or similar, glossing that {X,Y} has an inf.
In the last Proposition: 'On ne suppose pas F ≭ G, soit L = F.G. Alors F ≭ G si les conditions suivantes sont satisfaites'.
